questions.question: Why do bread becomes rough and dry on storage? / [CO2, CO3, CO5]
questions.solution_html:
• Why do bread becomes rough and dry on storage? [A] / [CO2, CO3, CO5]
  • Bread becomes rough and dry due to starch retrogradation, where gelatinized starch
  • recrystallizes over time, leading to moisture redistribution and firm texture (staling).

questions.question: How do proteins act as emulsifying agents in food systems? / [CO2, CO3, CO5]
questions.solution_html:
• How do proteins act as emulsifying agents in food systems?[U] / [CO2, CO3, CO5]
  • Proteins contain both hydrophilic and hydrophobic groups, allowing them to adsorb at the
  • oil–water interface, reduce interfacial tension, and stabilize emulsions.

• Explain the concept of antioxidant synergism[U] / [CO1, CO2]

questions.question: What are non starch polysaccharides? Give it's application in food. / [CO2, CO3, CO5]
questions.solution_html:
• What are non-starch polysaccharides? Give its application in food.[U] / [CO2, CO3, CO5]

  • hemicellulose, pectin, and gums.Applications: act as dietary fiber, thickening agents, stabilizers,

questions.question: Describe the effect of temperature, p H, metal ions and oxygen on enzymatic browning. / [CO2]
questions.solution_html:
• Describe the effect of temperature, pH, metal ions and oxygen on enzymatic browning.[U] / [CO2]
  • • Temperature: increases enzyme activity up to optimum, then denatures enzyme
  • • pH: acidic pH inhibits enzyme activity
  • • Metal ions: Cu²⁺ activates polyphenol oxidase
  • • Oxygen: essential for oxidation reactions leading to browning

questions.question: Define rancidity. Discuss about different types of rancidity. / [CO1, CO2]
questions.solution_html:
• Define rancidity. Discuss about different types of rancidity.[K] / [CO1, CO2]
  • Rancidity is the deterioration of fats and oils resulting in unpleasant odor and taste.
  • Types:
  • • Oxidative rancidity (reaction with oxygen)
  • • Hydrolytic rancidity (lipase activity)
  • • ketonic rancidity

questions.question: Describe the different methods and products of starch hydrolysis and its important applications in food. / [CO2, CO3, CO5]

questions.question: Define amylase enzymes and explain its types along with its functions. / [CO2]
questions.solution_html:
• Define amylase enzymes and explain its types along with its functions.[U] / [CO2]
  • Amylases are enzymes that hydrolyze starch into simpler sugars.
  • Types:
  • • α-amylase: breaks internal α-1,4 bonds
  • • β-amylase: releases maltose from ends
  • • Glucoamylase: produces glucose
  • Functions:Used in the digestion, brewing, baking, and starch processing industries.
questions.source_exam: MGU-UGP (HONOURS) 2024 Admission Regular Exam Sem 4, March 2026

questions.question: Explain the procedure to determine peroxide value with calculations and discuss it's importance in assessing rancidity. / [CO2]
questions.solution_html:
• Explain the procedure to determine peroxide value with calculations and discuss it's
  • importance in assessing rancidity.[U] / [CO2]
  • Procedure:
  • • React fat sample with potassium iodide
  • • Liberated iodine titrated with sodium thiosulfate
  • Calculation:
  • Peroxide value = (S − B) × N × 1000 / W
  • Importance:
  • Indicates extent of oxidative rancidity and quality of fats.

questions.question: Discuss the structure and modifications of cellulose in food products. / [CO2, CO3, CO5] [10x2 = 20]
questions.solution_html:
• Discuss the structure and modifications of cellulose in food products.[U] / [CO2, CO3, CO5]
  • Structure:Cellulose is a linear polymer of β-1,4 linked glucose units forming strong fibers.
  • Modifications:Carboxymethyl cellulose (CMC) and Microcrystalline cellulose
  • Applications:
  • Used as thickener, stabilizer, fat replacer, and dietary fiber in food products.
